external_documentation.scope: General official API explanation of demand-created minimum threads and throughput-driven creation/destruction; exact implementation findings above use the installed package repository commit.

findings.fact: The default idle timeout is 20000 milliseconds of no work, configurable by System.Threading.ThreadPool.ThreadTimeoutMs / DOTNET_ThreadPool_ThreadTimeoutMs. This is not a wall-clock deadline from the end of external HTTP load.
The default minimum worker count derives from Environment.ProcessorCount. Minimum worker count does not cap worker creation; the source separately maintains a larger maximum.
Hill-climbing updates the active worker goal using sampled elapsed time and completions, injecting additional workers when that goal rises.
ThreadsToKeepAlive defaults to zero; explicit configuration can change worker retention. No such runtime-setting change is proposed.

Idle timeout does not unconditionally terminate a worker: pending IO and concurrent processing-count changes can keep it alive. Retirement decreases existing-worker count and updates the hill-climbing goal.
The worker implementation explicitly permits existing threads above the current active goal while cold workers wait to time out.

Blocking compensation can add ProcessorCount workers beyond the minimum without delay by default, and may add further workers with increasing delay. The immediate allowance is not a hard cap on the pool.

interpretation: An empirical total-thread maximum or one observed ThreadPool count is not a source-enforced invariant.
The completed120-second diagnostic classifies ThreadPool worker growth and persistent SQLx pool workers; it does not prove a new universal cap.

A small practical ThreadPool/extra-DB-worker budget must be independently predeclared as a qualification envelope and retained as an observational bound, not attributed to the runtime as a hard maximum.

The reviewer-owned proposed residual budget (peak9, idle6 for .NET TP workers plus DB workers above the four async workers) is separate from this source supplement. This supplement proposes no acceptance-cap change.

Keep per-owner thread classification, unknown-role rejection, source/Server retirement, qualified idle observations, and original failed frozen profiles. Do not change default ThreadPool settings to force a pass.

local_source_facts.fact: Each database Source owns one nw-db-owner thread, two async nw-db-worker threads and a maximum of four additional blocking threads; two reference sources therefore imply two owner threads, four async workers and at most eight additional DB blocking workers.

Business SQLite permits16 physical connections and the independent consumer permits2. SQLx establishes a dedicated worker thread per physical SQLite connection; those pooled connections may remain open while logical native session counters are zero.
The live Server runner uses one named OS thread with a current-thread Tokio runtime.
Server Close creates a distinct named close-wait thread. Linux comm truncation can make its name match the live runner; lifecycle phase must distinguish their permitted overlap.
The outbox background loop continues through application-live idle, normally waiting one second between cycles.
The observer continues to schedule periodic sampling at1100ms and does not stop merely because HTTP load ends.
